speaker: Tess
text: Review of lab sample ingestion. Technicians scan tubes into a desktop station.

speaker: Jun
text: Peak is 120 samples a minute per lab, up to 30 labs. Labels stay traceable to the source instrument.

speaker: Tess
text: Does the current station work offline?

speaker: Ravi
text: Yes, queues scans locally for four hours. That is current behavior, not a new feature request.

speaker: Tess
text: New requirement: accepted scans reach the lab worklist in under two seconds on the LAN.

speaker: Mina
text: Duplicate scans must not create duplicate samples.

speaker: Jun
text: Use a client UUID per scan as the idempotency key.

speaker: Ravi
text: Accepted. UUID stays stable on retry; server rejects duplicate key.

speaker: Mina
text: If we were Netflix, we would need global edge ingest and a data lake for every click.

speaker: Tess
text: That is an analogy, not a proposal. We have a few labs and regulated records.

speaker: Ravi
text: Imagine a graph database, just to illustrate a flexible schema. I am not recommending it.

speaker: Jun
text: We do not need a graph. Relational tables already cover sample, instrument, and assay.

speaker: Mina
text: Sure, let us just rewrite it in Rust, that will definitely fix the barcode printer.

speaker: Tess
text: Sarcasm noted. No rewrite decision.

speaker: Ravi
text: Transport from station to lab service: HTTPS batch endpoint over facility network.

speaker: Jun
text: Could use MQTT since instruments already speak it.

speaker: Ravi
text: Those instruments talk to station, not our service. Station can post HTTPS.

speaker: Tess
text: Agreed, HTTPS batch API, station is the client.

speaker: Mina
text: Should batch endpoint be synchronous?

speaker: Jun
text: Yes, return accepted IDs synchronously; persistence is complete before 200.

speaker: Mina
text: Okay, that answers it. Not an open question.

speaker: Ravi
text: Managed Postgres in each region, encrypted backups.

speaker: Tess
text: Could be one central database?

speaker: Jun
text: Latency and facility isolation argue regional. Records stay in assigned region.

speaker: Tess
text: Accepted, one regional Postgres per lab region.

speaker: Mina
text: Maybe add Redis for worklist?

speaker: Ravi
text: Not needed for measured load. Postgres index covers it.

speaker: Tess
text: Redis is only a suggestion, no cache decision.

speaker: Jun
text: Audit retention is seven years. Raw instrument payloads retained; normalized records queryable.

speaker: Mina
text: Could archive raw payloads to object storage after 90 days?

speaker: Tess
text: Real proposal, but not deciding storage tier today. Leave open.

speaker: Jun
text: I will get compliance retention and retrieval requirements by next Thursday.

speaker: Tess
text: Jun owns that follow-up.

speaker: Ravi
text: We also need an event bus. Maybe Kafka, unless the load test fails.

speaker: Tess
text: Plan on Kafka unless the load test fails; mark tentative until test.

speaker: Mina
text: I would start with direct Postgres writes and add a bus only if needed.

speaker: Jun
text: Endpoint can write Postgres and publish accepted-scan events to existing lab Kafka.

speaker: Tess
text: Tentative shape, still gated by load test.

speaker: Ravi
text: Fine, Kafka is probably okay.

speaker: Mina
text: Hold on, no load test for fanout and platform cannot support Kafka on lab network this quarter.

speaker: Mina
text: I object to calling Kafka the plan. Keep it undecided until platform confirms support; direct writes remain baseline.

speaker: Tess
text: Agreed, Kafka is not accepted. Open question whether supported event bus is available after load test.

speaker: Jun
text: I will ask platform about supported lab event transport by Friday.

speaker: Ravi
text: Worklist updates can poll every second?

speaker: Mina
text: That is a lot of queries. Use server-sent events?

speaker: Tess
text: Keep v1 simple, manual refresh plus 15 second poll. Accepted.

speaker: Jun
text: Then no live event stream in diagram.

speaker: Ravi
text: Deploy with Kubernetes?

speaker: Tess
text: Existing platform runs services on Kubernetes, no new platform decision.

speaker: Mina
text: Jun compliance retention next Thursday; Jun platform transport by Friday.

speaker: Jun
text: Yes, both.

speaker: Tess
text: No action for the graph database example.

speaker: Ravi
text: Printer jammed again, sorry, not part of this design.

speaker: Tess
text: Correct. Anything else unresolved beyond storage tier and Kafka support?

speaker: Mina
text: No, and under-two-second LAN target is accepted.

speaker: Tess
text: Regional database failover stays within assigned region; no cross-region copy.

speaker: Jun
text: Retention policy is seven years for audit records; operations can retrieve archived raw payloads if compliance asks.

speaker: Ravi
text: We have not decided object storage transition. Jun still has to get required retrieval time.

speaker: Tess
text: Correct, keep storage tier open. The 15-second worklist poll stays accepted.

speaker: Jun
text: Closing, I will bring platform support and retention answers back.
